context: Wilde to Frank Harris, 26 September 1900, Elysee Palace Hotel. Not a letter but the signed assignment itself — the document the October quarrel is about. He assigns the plot and scenario of what became Mr and Mrs Daventry outright, against £175 he acknowledges receiving and had not in fact received in full.
quote:
Dear Frank, In consideration of the sum of £175, of which this is an acknowledgment, and as one fourth share of your profits from the play, I hereby assign to you absolutely the entire rights in the plot and scenario I laid before you last June: you to have full rights to deal with said plot and scenario as you choose.

The plot and scenario are those used in the play provisionally termed ‘Her Second Chance’.

Yours sincerely Oscar Wilde

Sept. 26.
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 30-31 - one bifolium of Elysee Palace Hotel paper: image 30 shows sides 1 and 2, image 31 side 3 and the blank side 4. Signed in full, 'Oscar Wilde', not 'Oscar' - the only Harris document in the folder where he does. The stamps: two impressed revenue stamps on side 1, one Pound and Seven Shillings and Sixpence, which is exactly the '27s.6d. worth of official-looking stamps' of the volume's footnote; they read through blind-embossed on the verso. There is also '27/6' in red pencil at the head, and further red-pencil figures, not in Wilde's hand and not identified. Title, and what the volume does to it: the play is ‘Her Second Chance’, in Wilde's own inverted commas and not underlined. The volume sets it in italic. This is the second clean instance of that conversion in this pass, after Carpenter's ‘Civilization — Cause and Cure’ at p. 1197 - so his practice for a title is quotation marks, and the printed italic is the editor's. Emphasis: no underlines anywhere. The dateline 'Sept. 26.' at the foot is not underlined; it carries a paraph, as does the signature. Punctuation: 'last June: you to have' - his colon and lower case, where the volume gives a full stop and a capital.
